summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a patient with refractory multiple myeloma, COPD, and a history of bladder cancer with neobladder, was admitted from clinic due to worsening shortness of breath and hypoxia. He had been scheduled for cyclophosphamide infusion but presented feeling unwell. Imaging revealed new lung nodules and bronchial thickening concerning for infection, though viral testing was negative. He was treated with levofloxacin for pneumonia and initially received linezolid for a urinary tract infection caused by Enterobacter cloacae and Enterococcus; this was later de-escalated to amoxicillin based on sensitivities. His renal function, which was impaired on admission, improved with supportive care. He remained stable without hypoxia, and his blood counts normalized. He was discharged home on oral antibiotics, with instructions to continue COPD and myeloma-related medications, monitor weight, and follow up with his oncologist.
